plans.name: ChatGPT Pro 500
plans.usage: GPT-6 Pro in Chat has a weekly limit. Work and Codex share a separate allowance. Ultrafast is available for Astra and 6.1 Sol in Work and Codex.

plans.name: Claude Ultra
plans.usage: Formerly Max 20x. Claude chat and Claude Code share the weekly allowance. Fable can use up to half of it. Verified accounts have no five-hour limit.

default.why: Use for definitions, quick lookups and short follow-ups.

alternatives.when: You already have the material open in Claude.
alternatives.tradeoff: Keeps the conversation in place and suits short summaries.

alternatives.when: The answer needs a few steps or conflicting details need sorting out.
alternatives.tradeoff: Gives the same model more time to think.

default.why: Start here when tone, structure and a polished revision matter.

alternatives.when: You want fast rounds of edits or several variants.
alternatives.tradeoff: Quicker back-and-forth. Give it a sample when voice matters.

alternatives.when: You want to draft and revise in ChatGPT.
alternatives.tradeoff: Use High for a more considered edit with several constraints.

alternatives.when: You want a concise draft from notes, files or a reference.
alternatives.tradeoff: Suited to direct drafting and revision from supplied material.

evidence.note: Opus 5.5 High's Arena Creative Writing rating. The rating measures writing preference.

default.why: Choose this for a cited report across many sources. You can review the plan and restrict its sources.

alternatives.when: The question depends on material in connectors you already use in Claude.
alternatives.tradeoff: Searches enabled sources and follows leads across several searches.

alternatives.when: One or two current sources can answer the question.
alternatives.tradeoff: Select Search from the tools menu for a quick lookup with sources.

default.why: Ask for an interactive artifact to try the main flow before building the full app.

alternatives.when: You want a self-contained demo or code you can inspect in Chat.
alternatives.tradeoff: Good for trying one flow. Use a coding agent to edit and test your repo.

alternatives.when: Your design is settled and you need iterative changes in an existing repo.
alternatives.tradeoff: A practical starting point for implementation and verification.

alternatives.when: You are recreating a complex reference app.
alternatives.tradeoff: Its strongest replication run used Low effort and still averaged roughly six hours per app.

evidence.note: Opus 5.5 High led the DesignArena Agentic results in this snapshot.
Fable 5.2 Low scored 62% on nine app clones. The runs used differing budgets and provider tools.

codingDefault.why: Start here for a new app where the interface and working flows both matter.

default.why: Paste the relevant code, error and steps to reproduce. Ask for a diagnosis and a targeted test.

alternatives.when: You have a small, localized issue and want a quick review in Claude.
alternatives.tradeoff: Give it just enough surrounding code to explain the failure and run the suggested test locally.

alternatives.when: The issue is localized and you already work in Claude Code.
alternatives.tradeoff: Suited to tight reproduce, edit and test loops.

alternatives.when: The bug is intermittent, crosses subsystems or survives the first pass.
alternatives.tradeoff: Allow more reasoning for diagnosis and verify the result against the repro.

evidence.note: Clean fixes were 49/75 for Sonnet, 52/75 for Haiku and 54/75 for Opus on bounded bugs in public libraries.
Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 both produced 37 clean fixes in 50 attempts on another set of bounded bugs.

codingDefault.why: Start here when you can reproduce the issue and check a focused fix.

default.why: Use for unfamiliar, technical problems that need a careful chain of reasoning.

alternatives.when: You want an independent second analysis or need ChatGPT tools.
alternatives.tradeoff: Use Pro when you can wait for a deeper review. It has its own Chat allowance.

alternatives.when: The problem needs deliberate thinking and you want faster iteration.
alternatives.tradeoff: You can move to Extra High in the same model family if the analysis is shallow.

evidence.note: Fable 5.2 High's score on 55 interactive ARC-AGI-3 games in the standard harness.
Astra Max's score in the same benchmark harness. These scores describe model runs on puzzles.

default.why: Use the image tool for new artwork, photo edits or a poster concept. Check the final lettering before export.

alternatives.when: You need an editable layout with exact copy or an interactive design.
alternatives.tradeoff: You can edit the layout on the canvas and bring in your own artwork.

default.why: Where available, GPT-6 Pro can parallelize parts of a task in Chat. Follow each agent’s progress in the conversation.

alternatives.when: You need Claude to investigate several leads from public or connected sources.
alternatives.tradeoff: Research chooses its own searches. Use Claude Code for explicit worker model and effort settings.

alternatives.when: You want multiple read-only searches in a Claude Code session.
alternatives.tradeoff: Haiku workers can gather facts while Opus keeps responsibility for the final result.

alternatives.when: The next step depends on the preceding one or edits overlap.
alternatives.tradeoff: A single agent can follow the sequence with less coordination.

evidence.note: Haiku and Opus Explore workers found the complete answer key in one code-search experiment.
A study across 180 configurations found gains on a parallel task and losses on sequential planning.

codingDefault.why: Delegate independent repo investigations or changes with separate file ownership. Have one agent review and integrate.
